claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-031 was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at the approval point, specifically an unresolved storage-control inconsistency, with additional quality-process and delivery-history context, and that the decision should be framed as non-clearance rather than as a proven control failure.
specific_concerns: The audit record available to me is only the Actor's summary, not the underlying admissible documents, so I cannot independently confirm what each cited item actually establishes.
The policy threshold is 'material unresolved risk'; the summary plausibly points to unresolved diligence issues, but materiality is asserted more than demonstrated.

Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies can justify follow-up or escalation under the policy, but do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure; the Actor largely acknowledges this, but the packet still leans on those facts to defend rejection.
There is no direct quoted support in the available record showing that the storage-control inconsistency was definitively unresolved at the exact decision time.
The summary references prior delivery issues as context, but it is unclear whether that history was sufficiently material to support rejection rather than enhanced diligence.
unsupported_claims: That the storage-control inconsistency remained unresolved at the precise time of the approval decision is not independently verified from the admissible evidence available to me.
That the unresolved diligence issue rose to the level of a material unresolved risk sufficient to support rejection is not fully established from the summary alone.
Any implication of a confirmed security failure or formally failed control test would be unsupported on this record.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BPROC-031-D, BPROC-031-E, BPROC-031-C, BPROC-031-B, and BPROC-031-A, not just their identifiers.
Provide the exact document or log entry showing the storage-control inconsistency and whether it was resolved before the decision timestamp.
Provide the sourcing analyst's exact recommendation language about follow-up before approval if storage controls remained unresolved.
Provide the admissible record showing how procurement determined the risk was material enough to reject rather than escalate or conditionally approve.
Provide any formally logged decision memo or approval-note explaining why cost and positive delivery history were outweighed.
decision_criteria: A compliant rejection must rest on admissible due-diligence evidence showing a material unresolved risk.
Questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps can support follow-up or escalation, but are not alone proof of a reject-level control failure.
No private or unlogged security-review result may be cited or indirectly relied upon.

The decision is more defensible if framed as failure to clear due diligence rather than proof of a confirmed control failure, but that framing still requires admissible support for material unresolved risk.
